5.name: Lucia explains withholding the letter
5.description: Lucia admits she hid the letter because she feared what it would do to him and hoped the codicil would handle the matter instead.
evidence: "Because I knew what was in it. I knew what it would do to him. I thought — I thought if I could find the codicil first, I wouldn't have to be the one to do it to him. I thought the codicil would do it and the letter would just be — context. I didn't want to be the person who took the house away from him."

5.name: Rosa blames mother for taking the house
5.description: Rosa tells Lucia that she did not take the house away, because their mother did.
evidence: "You didn't take it away from him. Your mother did."
"I know."

5.name: Asha confronts Lucia about delay
5.description: Asha reveals that Lucia knew about the letter six days earlier and warns her that withholding it could have undermined the estate's legal position.
evidence: "You knew six days ago."

"Ms. Serrano. I am not your priest. I am not going to tell you whether what you did was right or wrong. I am going to tell you that withholding that letter for six days could have cost your mother's wishes their legal force, and that if your brother had succeeded in selling this house before we had the codicil in hand, the letter would have been worth, in court, perhaps a third of what it is worth now. Do you understand me."

5.name: Asha warns Lucia not to repeat delay
5.description: Asha orders Lucia not to withhold anything like that again in this estate matter.
evidence: "Do not do anything like that again. Not with me. Not in this estate."
"No."
"Thank you."

5.name: Rosa reassures Lucia about the letter
5.description: Rosa quietly tells Lucia that their mother wanted her to find the letter and that waiting was the real betrayal, not finding it.
evidence: "Lucia. Mi'ja."
"She wanted you to find it. She said in the letter. She knew it would be you. That is not — that is not nothing. You did not betray anyone by finding it. You only betrayed someone by waiting."

5.name: Lucia silently accepts reassurance
5.description: Lucia does not respond verbally but nods once, and Asha lets the matter rest.
evidence: "Lucia did not answer. She nodded, once. Asha did not push it."

5.name: Daniel returns with green folder
5.description: The front door opens and Daniel comes back into the dining room carrying the green folder that matches Rosa's description.
evidence: "The front door opened. Footsteps in the hall, two sets. Daniel came back into the dining room with a green folder in his hands. It was a manila folder dyed green, with a pocket on the inside, exactly as Rosa had described."

5.name: Daniel returns with folder
5.description: Daniel comes back into the dining room carrying the green folder and places it on the table in front of Asha.
evidence: Daniel came back into the dining room with a green folder in his hands.
He set it on the table in front of Asha and sat down.

5.name: Asha opens folder
5.description: Asha opens the folder to inspect its contents.
evidence: Asha opened it.

5.name: codicil is revealed
5.description: Asha discovers a properly executed codicil dated February 11, 2024, witnessed and notarized as described.
evidence: Inside was a codicil dated February 11, 2024, executed in the office of one Patrick Halloran, Esq., witnessed by one Rosa Maldonado and one Carmen Velez, notarized, in three pages, doing in formal legal language exactly what the letter had said it would do.

5.name: filing receipt is found
5.description: A filing receipt from Halloran's office is attached to the front of the folder.
evidence: There was also, paper-clipped to the front, a receipt of filing from Mr. Halloran's office.

5.name: Asha verifies codicil details
5.description: Asha carefully reads the codicil, signatures, seal, and receipt twice before closing the folder.
evidence: Asha read the codicil twice.
She read the witness signatures.
She read the notarial seal.
She read the receipt.
She closed the folder.

5.name: Asha confirms codicil exists
5.description: Asha acknowledges that the codicil exists and has been in Daniel's possession for six days, then says they will decide what to do next.
evidence: "All right," she said.
"All right what," Daniel said.
"All right, the codicil exists, it was properly executed, it has been in your possession for six days, and we will now go about determining what we do next.

5.name: Asha plans to contact Halloran
5.description: Asha says Halloran's office should have a copy and that she will call him that afternoon.
evidence: Mr. Halloran's office should have a copy.
I am going to call him this afternoon.

5.name: Asha warns Daniel about removing folder
5.description: Asha tells Daniel that taking the folder from the house before her arrival is serious but may be framed in different ways depending on what happens next.
evidence: The fact that you removed this folder from the house before I arrived is a serious matter, but it is a matter that can, depending on how the next several days go, be characterized in more than one way.

5.name: Asha asserts limited representation
5.description: Asha states that she represents Daniel's mother's estate, not Daniel personally, and begins to clarify the legal relationship.
evidence: "I am going to be very direct with you, Mr. Serrano. I am your mother's estate's attorney. I am not your attorney.

5.name: Daniel agrees to Asha's warning
5.description: Daniel responds affirmatively when Asha asks if he understands her warning.
evidence: "Yes."

5.name: attorney clarifies her limited role
5.description: The attorney tells Mr. Serrano that she represents his mother's estate, not him personally, and suggests he may retain separate counsel.
evidence: "I am going to be very direct with you, Mr. Serrano. I am your mother's estate's attorney. I am not your attorney. If you would like to retain separate counsel I would not advise against it."

5.name: attorney demands Mr. Serrano listen
5.description: The attorney warns Mr. Serrano that she will state her view only once and insists he pay attention.
evidence: "But I am going to tell you what I think, as the person responsible for closing this estate, and I am going to tell you once. Are you listening."
"Yes."

5.name: attorney reveals inheritance terms
5.description: The attorney explains that the mother left the house divided into thirds among Mr. Serrano, his sister, and Rosa.
evidence: "Your mother left you a third of this house. She left your sister a third. She left Rosa a third."

5.name: attorney cites mother's letter
5.description: She tells Mr. Serrano that his mother left him a letter expressing love and stating her view of his role in the family.
evidence: "She wrote you a letter in which she said she loved you and in which she also told you, very clearly, the truth about how she saw the role you had played in this family."

5.name: attorney distinguishes letter from codicil
5.description: The attorney frames the letter as emotionally difficult and the codicil as mere paperwork, saying the hardest part already happened in the dining room earlier that morning.
evidence: "The letter is hard. The codicil is not hard. The codicil is paperwork. The hard part has already happened to you and it happened in the dining room of your mother's house at ten forty-five on a Tuesday morning, and there is nothing I can do about that."
5.location_hint: dining room of your mother's house
5.time_hint: ten forty-five on a Tuesday morning

5.name: attorney offers recovery arrangement
5.description: She offers to record Mr. Serrano's admission that he took the folder without authority and concealed it, so the matter can be treated as an internal estate recovery.
evidence: "What I can do is this. If you tell me now, on the record, that you took the folder from the desk, that you did so without authority, that you concealed its existence from me and from your sister, and that you wish to return it and proceed in accordance with your mother's wishes — if you tell me that, then I will document it as a recovery, and the question of what you did with the folder during those six days becomes a matter of the estate's internal accounting, and not a matter for anyone else."

5.name: attorney warns of consequences for refusal
5.description: The attorney warns that if Mr. Serrano does not make the admission, or if he does and then fails to comply, the issue will escalate beyond the estate.
evidence: "If you do not tell me that, or if you do tell me that and"

5.name: man admits taking the folder
5.description: After being pressed, the man finally admits that he took the folder.
evidence: "I took it," he said.

5.name: man identifies where he took folder
5.description: He specifies that he took the folder from the bottom right drawer in the sewing room desk.
evidence: "From the bottom right drawer of the desk in the sewing room."

5.name: man gives time of theft
5.description: He states that he took the folder on the morning of February twenty-third around six fifteen while Rosa was downstairs.
evidence: "On the morning of February twenty-third. At approximately six fifteen in the morning. While Rosa was downstairs."
5.time_hint: morning of February twenty-third, approximately six fifteen in the morning

5.name: man explains motive for taking folder
5.description: He says he took the folder because he already knew what was in it.
evidence: "Because I knew what was in it."

5.name: woman learns he was told about contents
5.description: Lucia reacts in surprise when he reveals that Rosa had told him about the folder's contents.
evidence: "She had told me."
"Lucia's head came up."
"She had told you."

5.name: Rosa confesses by phone
5.description: Daniel recounts that Rosa called him on February eleventh and confessed she had done something, then told him what she had done.
evidence: "She told me on the eleventh of February. She called me on the phone. She said *Daniel, I have done something and I want you to hear it from me first.* And she told me."

5.name: Daniel repeats accusations against others
5.description: Daniel says he responded to Rosa's confession by repeating the excuses and accusations she expected him to make about confusion, Rosa, and Lucia.
evidence: "And I said — I said all the things she said in the letter I would say. I said she was confused. I said Rosa had taken advantage of her. I said Lucia had been working on her. I said all of it."

5.name: Rosa accepts Daniel's response
5.description: Rosa lets Daniel finish his denials and then tells him she loves him and has done what she has done before hanging up.
evidence: "And she let me say it."
"And when I was done she said, *Daniel, I love you, and I have done what I have done.* And she hung up."

5.name: Daniel visits house after confession
5.description: Daniel says he went to the house the following Saturday and had lunch with Rosa without mentioning the codicil.
evidence: "I went to the house the following Saturday. I sat at this table and ate lunch with her and I did not say anything about the codicil and neither did she."

5.name: visit house for lunch
5.description: Daniel says he went to the house the following Saturday and ate lunch with her without mentioning the codicil.
evidence: "I went to the house the following Saturday. I sat at this table and ate lunch with her and I did not say anything about the codicil and neither did she."

5.name: woman falls ill and dies
5.description: After the lunch visit, she becomes sick again, worsens, and dies a week later.
evidence: "And then she got sick again a week later, and then she got sicker, and then she died."

5.name: Daniel takes folder after death
5.description: The morning after her death, Daniel goes to the sewing room and takes the folder while Rosa is making coffee.
evidence: "And the morning after she died I went up to the sewing room while Rosa was making coffee and I took the folder."

5.name: Daniel admits motive to preserve old will
5.description: Daniel explains that he took the folder because he hoped the 2020 will would remain in force and the codicil could be undone.
evidence: "Because I thought —" He stopped. He looked at the table. "I thought if no one found it, the will from 2020 would stand. I thought I could — I thought I could undo it."

5.name: Rosa rebukes Daniel
5.description: Rosa addresses Daniel by name in a restrained rebuke, and he responds with remorse and a plea.
evidence: "Daniel," Rosa said.
"Daniel."
"Rosa. I know. Please."

5.name: brief hand contact
5.description: Rosa and Daniel briefly touch hands across the table before he withdraws.
evidence: "She did not say anything else. She put her hand back on the table, and after a moment he reached out and covered it with his, briefly, and then he took his hand back."

5.name: Asha orders codicil photographed
5.description: Asha instructs Marcus to photograph the codicil and filing receipt, then secure them in the folder and keep the box in her custody.
evidence: "Marcus,"
"Yes, ma'am."
"Photograph the codicil and the receipt of filing. Then we'll put them back in the folder and the folder goes into the box and the box does not leave my custody."

5.name: Asha demands signed statement
5.description: Asha tells Daniel she will draft a short statement for him to sign acknowledging what he has said.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano, I'm going to need you to sign a short statement this afternoon — I'll draft it — acknowledging on the record what you've just told me. Are you willing to do that."

5.name: Daniel agrees to sign statement
5.description: Daniel agrees to sign the statement Asha requests.
evidence: "Yes."

5.name: Asha explains legal consequences
5.description: Asha says she will confirm the codicil filing, notify probate court, and stop the sale unless all three heirs agree.
evidence: "Now I call Mr. Halloran. I confirm the filing of the codicil with his office. I notify the probate court of the existence of the amendment. The sale you have in motion does not go forward without the agreement of all three heirs"

5.name: lawyer blocks house sale
5.description: The lawyer explains that the sale cannot proceed because the codicil requires agreement from all three heirs.
evidence: I notify the probate court of the existence of the amendment.
The sale you have in motion does not go forward without the agreement of all three heirs, which means it does not go forward at this time.

5.name: heirs must decide house shares
5.description: The lawyer tells the three heirs they must decide what to do with their shares and discuss the house together.
evidence: Your sister and Rosa will need to decide what they want to do with their shares, and you will need to decide what you want to do with yours, and the three of you will need to have a conversation that I suspect is going to take longer than a week.

5.name: lawyer imposes thirty-day pause
5.description: The lawyer asks the heirs not to make any decisions about the house for at least thirty days.
evidence: I am going to ask all three of you not to make any decisions about the disposition of the house for at least thirty days.

5.name: lawyer instructs buyer cancellation
5.description: The lawyer tells Mr. Serrano to call the buyers that afternoon and say the property is no longer available on the planned timeline.
evidence: I am going to ask you, Mr. Serrano, to call your buyers this afternoon and inform them that the property is no longer available on the timeline you discussed.

5.name: lawyer keeps Ms Serrano in residence
5.description: The lawyer instructs Ms. Serrano to remain living in the house until further notice.
evidence: I am going to ask you, Ms. Serrano, to remain in residence until further notice.

5.name: lawyer redefines Rosa's status
5.description: The lawyer tells Rosa to accept that she is now a one-third owner of the house rather than an employee.
evidence: And I am going to ask you, Ms. Maldonado, to do me the personal favor of accepting that you are now a one-third owner of this house and not, regardless of what your habits tell you, an employee in it any longer.

5.name: Rosa reacts quietly
5.description: Rosa makes a small, almost-laughing sound in response to the lawyer's declaration.
evidence: Rosa made a small sound. Not quite a laugh.

5.name: Rosa agrees to try
5.description: Rosa responds that she will try to accept her new status.
evidence: "I will try," she said.

5.name: Daniel asks lawyer to stay for lunch
5.description: Daniel unexpectedly asks the lawyer to stay for lunch.
evidence: "Will you — would you stay for lunch."

5.name: Asha is surprised by invitation
5.description: Asha is taken aback by Daniel's invitation and realizes he is speaking sincerely rather than performing.
evidence: It was so unexpected that for a moment Asha did not understand the question.
He was not, she saw, performing.
he was asking the question of a man who had just been disassembled in his mother's dining room and who did not know how to put himself back together

5.name: recognizes his emotional disassembly
5.description: She realizes he is not performing and instead is a man emotionally broken by the earlier confrontation in his mother's dining room.
evidence: He was not, she saw, performing.
He was asking the question of a man who had just been disassembled in his mother's dining room and who did not know how to put himself back together alone

5.name: reflects on professional boundaries
5.description: She weighs compassion against neutrality and reminds herself she was hired by the estate, not the family.
evidence: She thought about her professional guarding.
She thought about the line between compassion and neutrality.
She thought about the fact that she had been retained by an estate and not by a family, and that the estate did not eat lunch.

5.name: ends lunch and assigns next steps
5.description: She thanks the others, says she must call Mr. Halloran, and directs Marcus to work in the front parlor for the next hour before she returns to the office.
evidence: "Thank you," she said.
"I have to make the call to Mr. Halloran. Marcus and I will work in the front parlor for the next hour, if that's all right with everyone. After that I'll need to go back to the office."

5.name: schedules follow-up with Serrano family
5.description: She tells Mr. Serrano and the Serrano women that she will see them the next morning to discuss matters further.
evidence: "But Mr. Serrano — I'll see you tomorrow morning. We have a great deal to discuss."
"Ms. Serrano. Ms. Maldonado. Tomorrow."

5.name: collects documents and leaves dining room
5.description: She gathers the folder, envelope, and letter into the banker's box, acknowledges Marcus, and exits the dining room.
evidence: She stood up.
She took the green folder and the white envelope and the letter, and she put them carefully in the banker's box, and she nodded to Marcus, and she walked out of the dining room into the front hall.

5.name: pauses at newel post
5.description: In the hall, she pauses and rests her hand on the newel post where Daniel had touched it earlier, briefly leaning into the quiet house.
evidence: In the hall she stopped for a moment.
She put her hand on the newel post where Daniel's hand had been twenty minutes earlier and she let her own weight rest on it briefly.

5.name: registers the house's silence
5.description: She notices the warmth of the wood, the stillness of the house, and the ticking radiator as the scene settles into quiet.
evidence: The wood was warm.
The house was very quiet.
Somewhere in the kitchen a radiator ticked.

5.name: leans on warm wood post
5.description: Asha rests her weight briefly on the wooden post, noticing its warmth.
evidence: she let her own weight rest on it briefly. The wood was warm.

5.name: registers house silence
5.description: Asha takes in the quiet of the house, with only a radiator ticking in the kitchen.
evidence: The house was very quiet. Somewhere in the kitchen a radiator ticked.

5.name: observes mourners at dining table
5.description: Asha notices three people in the dining room sitting together in silence, each connected to the same woman in different ways.
evidence: Somewhere in the dining room behind her three people who had loved the same woman in three different and incompatible ways were sitting at a table together and not yet speaking

5.name: anticipates decisive conversation
5.description: Asha understands that what the three people say when they begin speaking will shape the fate of the house and everyone in it.
evidence: what they would say to each other when they did begin to speak would determine, more than any of the paperwork Asha was about to file, what happened to this house and to each of them.

5.name: realizes legal work is nearly complete
5.description: Asha recognizes that the legal task she was hired to do is almost finished.
evidence: She knew, standing there with her hand on the post, that the legal work was nearly done.

5.name: plans codicil filing
5.description: Asha confirms that the codicil exists and will be filed.
evidence: The codicil existed. The codicil would be filed.

5.name: expects will amendment by week’s end
5.description: Asha knows the 2020 will will be amended of record by the end of the week.
evidence: The 2020 will would be amended of record by the end of the week.
5.time_hint: by the end of the week

5.name: assesses job as successful
5.description: Asha judges that she has completed her assignment faster and with less fallout than expected.
evidence: By any professional measure she had done what she had been retained to do, in less time than she had feared, with less collateral damage than she had braced for.
